quotes.text: A session is how the workspace keeps one customer issue together. Think of it like a labeled desk draw.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable analogy that explains the core multisession concept.

quotes.text: That is what OmniChannel means in plain English. The company lets customers choose how to get in touch, while service agents work from the same place.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines omnichannel service in one plain-English sentence.

quotes.text: Still, a draft is a starting point, not a final decision. The agent checks the facts, the tone, the customer details, any promises made, nothing leaves the company until the agent reviews it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear human-in-the-loop rule for using Copilot drafts in customer service.

quotes.text: It's asking who has the right skill is available to take work and isn't already overloaded. That creates a much smarter path for customer requests.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises how routing weighs skills, presence and capacity.

quotes.text: Prepared text saves typing. It doesn't remove responsibility. The agent still needs to read it before sending every time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise reminder that templates and quick replies still need human review.

chapters.title: Sessions and tabs: the desk drawer analogy
The productivity pane, Smart Assist and knowledge
Scripts, macros, quick replies and Copilot

takeaways: Copilot Service workspace, formerly Customer Service workspace, keeps each customer issue in its own session with up to ten tabs, so agents stop rebuilding context.
Omnichannel channels, cases, timelines, the productivity pane, scripts, macros and Copilot help agents find answers fast, but people still review everything before it is sent.
Behind the scenes unified routing uses queues, skills, presence and capacity, while SLA timers, escalation rules and dashboards help teams keep promises and spot patterns.
hook: Customer service agents lose time jumping between inboxes, tabs and notes while customers repeat their story. This Simply Explained episode is for Dynamics 365 users, service leads and admins who want to understand how Copilot Service workspace organizes sessions, channels, knowledge, Copilot help and unified routing in one service desk.
